Stone Description: Dover White is a dolomitic marble from Namibia with a white to soft cream base, cloud-like warm taupe and pale grey movement and fine branching veins, suited to bookmatched feature walls, bathroom cladding, vanity tops and pool halls.
Overview: Dover White, also sold as Oyster White, is a fine-grained dolomitic marble quarried in Namibia. The slab reads as a white to soft cream field broken by broad, cloud-like areas of warm taupe and pale grey, with finer veins branching through the whiter zones. Because the movement is large in scale and shifts across a block, it is at its best where whole slabs can be seen: bookmatched walls, full-height bathroom cladding and long vanity runs. As a dolomitic marble it is generally denser and a little more resistant to etching than calcitic white marbles such as Carrara, though it still needs sealing and sensible care.
Colour: White, soft cream, warm taupe and pale grey
Veining / Movement: Broad cloud-like and oval movement with fine branching veins across a white to cream field
Finish Options: Polished, honed or leathered, subject to slab selection and application.
Applications: Bookmatched feature walls, Bathroom wall cladding, Vanity tops, Pool and spa walls
Design Notes: Dover White rewards slab-by-slab planning. The oval, cloud-like figures repeat from slab to slab within a block, so sequential slabs can be bookmatched into mirrored panels; at Dormans Park the pool hall walls were set out this way, and the principal bathroom uses the same stone at full height. Ask for slabs from one block and approve a dry-lay or digital layout before cutting, because the balance of warm taupe and cooler grey varies from slab to slab. It pairs well with bronze and aged brass, pale oak, limestone floors and warm white plaster.
